summary: Theodorus Willem Juynboll worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University (around 1886-1893) under Hendrik Arent Hamaker and later taught Jan Gonda, holding a post at Utrecht University in 1916.

Theofil Simenschy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University, earning his PhD in 1927. His career there included positions as Assistant (1926), Docent (1938), and Professor of Classical Languages and Comparative IE Philology (1942-1968).

Theophil Gubler was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Basel in 1903 under doctoral supervisor Jacob Wackernagel. He subsequently served as a teacher at Gymnasium am Münsterplatz from 1906 to 1934.

Theos Bernard worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned an L.L.B. from the University of Arizona and an M.A. and Ph.D. from Columbia University, completing his doctorate under Herbert Schneider in 1943.
Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist with a post at the University of Chicago. He is also attested as a Vertretungsprofessor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Thich Nhat Hanh was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. Educated at Báo Quốc Temple, University of Saigon, Columbia, Princeton, and Princeton Theological Seminary, he held posts at Columbia, Princeton, Vạn Hạnh University, and Cornell, and founded several institutions.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi (attested 2012) under the supervision of Shalini Singhal.

Thierry Mathou is a scholar in Tibetology. Educated at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, he has held a post as an Associated Political Scientist at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

Thierry Meynard is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who earned his PhD at Peking University (around 1999-2003) under Yulie Lou. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies.

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya and teachers Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.

Thinlay Ram Shashni is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He has served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as editor (attested 1997, 2007) and as Associate Professor, IN-charge/HoD (attested 2026).

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1994), and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Mindrolling Monastery under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje). He founded the White Lotus School and taught Albion Moonlight Butters, Chönyi Drolma, and Garab Dorje Rinpoche.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Georgetown (B.A.), Loyola University Chicago (M.A.), and the University of Chicago Divinity School (Ph.D. under Paul J. Griffiths), later teaching at Mercyhurst University.

Thomas A. Tweed is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Stanford University (around 1979-1984) under William R. Hutchison. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at UNC Chapel Hill from around 1993 to 2008.

Thomas Alexander Wise was an Indology and history scholar who earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh in 1824. He served in the Indian Medical Service (1827-1851) and founded Hooghly Mohsin College in 1834, serving as its Principal.
Thomas Andrew Lumisden Strange was an Indologist. He was educated at Westminster School and studied at the University of Oxford, earning a B.A. (around 1774-1778) and a D.C.L. in 1818.

Thomas Athol Joyce worked in history and archaeology. After attending Dulwich College and earning an M.A. from Hertford College, Oxford (around 1897-1902), he served as Deputy Keeper at the British Museum from 1902 to 1938.

Thomas B. Ellis is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He received his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

Thomas Best Jervis was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts with the East India Company (around 1813-1841), the Survey of India (around 1814-1841), and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.
